extracted.intended_audience: sovereigns, political ministers, clergy, and learned readers of political/theological philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance from a political-philosophical treatise on how Christian commonwealths should determine authority, interpret Scripture, recognize prophets, and prescribe the obligations of subjects and sovereigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereigns' necessary science: natural justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science of Naturall Justice is the onely Science necessary for Soveraigns, and their principall Ministers; other sciences (e.g., mathematics) are not required of them beyond what good laws should encourage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereigns should prioritize knowledge of natural justice and the principles needed to govern and secure obedience; other scholarly studies may be promoted by law but are not essential to the exercise of sovereignty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of senses and natural reason in religious-political matters
rubrics_metrics.description: We are not to renounce our Senses, and Experience; nor (that which is the undoubted Word of God) our naturall Reason. These are the talents God hath put into our hands to negotiate till the coming again of our Saviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation of Scripture and decisions about public religion must employ common sense, experience, and natural reason; mysteries beyond reason should not contradict reason, and where they seem to do so, the fault lies in poor interpretation or reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captivity of the understanding (what obedience requires)
rubrics_metrics.description: To Captivate our Understanding is not submission of the intellectual faculty to another's opinion, but of the Will to Obedience, where obedience is due. We captivate our Understanding when we forbear contradiction, speak as lawfull Authority commands, and live accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects may obey authoritative commands even when the mind lacks full comprehension; 'captivity' means refraining from public contradiction and acting as commanded while private assent of reason may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: How God may be said to speak and the limits of private revelation
rubrics_metrics.description: God can speak immediately or by mediation; claims of immediate divine speech (dreams, visions, inspiration) by private persons do not oblige others to belief or obedience unless supported by lawful authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A private person's assertion of immediate revelation is weak evidence: dreams and visions are commonly natural; inspiration may be mere ardent desire or arrogance. Only when the speaker has sovereign authority does obedience in practice become enforceable (though not necessarily internal belief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two marks of a true prophet
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two marks, joined together, by which a true Prophet is to be known: (1) the doing of miracles; and (2) the not teaching any other Religion than that which is already established. Asunder, neither is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate prophetic claims by requiring both conformity of doctrine to the established religion and demonstrable miracles. Either alone is insufficient: miracles may be performed by false prophets, and correct doctrine alone without miracles cannot prove immediate revelation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal proximity of miracles as confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: The miracles that oblige us to beleeve a Prophet ought to be confirmed by an immediate, or a not long deferr'd event; otherwise prophetic prediction separated by long or indefinite time is unuseful for testing truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess prophetic predictions by whether predicted events occur within a reasonable/observable timeframe; overly distant or indefinite fulfilments cannot reliably confirm a prophet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of miracles that incite revolt
rubrics_metrics.description: How great soever the miracle be, yet if it tend to stir up revolt against the King, or him that governeth by the King's authority, he that doth such miracle is not to be considered otherwise than as sent to make triall of their allegiance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Miraculous claims should be disregarded (or treated as tests of loyalty) when they encourage rebellion against lawful sovereign authority; political destabilization nullifies their religious weight in public order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceasing of miracles — Scripture as substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeing therefore Miracles now cease, we have no sign left whereby to acknowledge pretended Revelations; the Scriptures supply the want of Prophecy and from them, by wise and careful ratiocination, all necessary rules and precepts may be deduced without Enthusiasme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities and subjects should rely on Scripture (interpreted by reason) rather than on claimed contemporary miracles or private inspiration; avoid enthusiasm and supernaturalist claims as bases for public law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of canonical Books: sovereign/church establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Books of Holy SCRIPTURE, are understood those, which ought to be the Canon... those Books only are Canonicall, that is, Law, in every nation, which are established for such by the Soveraign Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine a community's canon by what the sovereign (or its established Church authority acting as sovereign within the dominion) has commanded to be acknowledged; canon is thus juridically instituted, not merely historically attributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of scriptural authority relative to natural law and promulgation
rubrics_metrics.description: As far as the Scriptures differ not from the Laws of Nature, they are the Law of God, legible to all men by naturall reason. If not so, their force as law depends on whether God has so sufficiently published them, or on the authority of the Common-wealth that makes them law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where scriptural precepts conform with natural reason they have universal moral authority; where they do not, the obligation to obey depends on either divine publication (for those specially revealed) or on the sovereign/commonwealth's legislative power within its territory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to interpret Scripture belongs to lawful sovereign power
rubrics_metrics.description: Whosoever hath a lawfull power over any Writing, to make it Law, hath the power also to approve, or disapprove the interpretation of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within a polity, the person or assembly possessing legitimate legislative/judicial power also has the authority to determine authoritative interpretations of Scripture for that commonwealth; interpretation is thus tied to political sovereignty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for judging signification of ambiguous words (e.g., body, spirit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation of true Ratiocination is the constant Signification of words; it is necessary... to determine, out of the Bible, the meaning of such words, as by their ambiguity may render inferences obscure or disputable (beginning with BODY and SPIRIT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For precise legal and theological reasoning, fix the meanings of ambiguous terms according to their sense in Scripture (and common use as relevant); clarifying terminology is a prerequisite for sound deductive argument about law and religion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical/linguistic tests for authorship and dating of biblical books
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments from internal phrases (e.g., 'unto this day') and references to earlier registers indicate that many books (Pentateuch, Joshua, Judges, Samuel, Kings, Chronicles) were written after the events they describe; titles do not prove authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing claims about authorship or antiquity, use internal textual marks, references to contemporary registers, and linguistic/formal features as evidence; do not assume traditional ascriptions (e.g., 'of Moses') are proof of contemporary composition.
